_comment: FROZEN cross-language parity corpus for the PRE-v3 witness layouts. Originally produced by the on-chain escrow program's own compute_*_hash functions; the Go encoder (parity_golden_test.go) and the TS encoder (parity-golden.test.ts) both assert against it. WHAT 'FROZEN' MEANS HERE, precisely: the HASHES AND INPUT VALUES are frozen -- do not regenerate them and never 'fix' a mismatch by editing them, because a mismatch means an encoder changed a frozen layout, which is the bug. The JSON KEY NAMES are not frozen: they track the Go/TS field names so the fixture stays readable next to the encoders it pins, and renaming one cannot change a hash. The deposit case's key was renamed payment_id -> deposit_request_hash on that basis, in the same commit as both readers. DO NOT confuse this with SolanaDepositPrehash, whose JSON key deliberately STAYS payment_id: that is a WIRE shape that producers emit and consumers parse, so renaming it would break them. This file is a test fixture -- it is excluded from the npm package (files: dist, src, and it sits above the package root), has no go:embed, and its only readers are the two in-repo tests. If it is ever published or embedded, the key names become a real contract and this paragraph stops applying. The program can no longer produce these values: compute_reserve_hash/release/refund now always bind quote_hash (domain v3, CORE-2022) and compute_deposit_hash now always binds destination_hash (domain v4, CORE-2120). These cases pin domain versions 1 and 2, so they are exactly what the FROZEN legacy encoder functions must keep reproducing for historical deposits. New layouts get new anchors instead - see v4_destination_test.go and v2_quotehash_test.go.
